This presents 5 core challenges:

No single source of truth & consistent and reliable view of performance: Board, management and operators do not have a reliable and consolidated view of financial performance, as there is no single source of truth platform & dataset. Therefore, the business is not able to track performance and progress against the value creation plan and identify opportunities to drive value across the business.

Lack of Consistent KPIs and Data Quality Issues: Current reporting does not always align with industry standard best practices, limiting confidence in decision making. Historic data is incomplete, and there are known data quality issues in subbranches, reducing the consistency of KPIs and reporting.

Limited financial reporting scalability: Each past acquisition contains additional datasets of varying quality, produced by different process and with nuanced definitions and logic. Therefore, a single source of truth data platform designed & optimized to support & scale with M&A is required.

Reporting dependency on system migrations: Acquired entities operate across different systems at and after the point of acquisition, with data sitting in multiple source systems prior to migration. Existing financial reporting leverages data from NetSuite, where some entities have not yet been migrated from QuickBooks. Migration timelines can take up to a year. This prevents rapid consolidated reporting across entities and create dependency on lengthy system migrations before reporting can be easily unified.

Lack of real time visibility into operational efficiency & process adherence: Management & operators are reliant on after-the-fact, manual reports and cannot drill down into operational metrics in real-time to support on-the-ground & rapid decision making. This limits the ability to monitor & identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, a key value lever for the business.

Currently, BP faces significant challenges in fully leveraging its data infrastructure to deliver accurate, streamlined financial reporting. The FP&A leadership is looking for support to efficiently progress financial data harmonisation and improve reconciliation, reporting accuracy, and forecasting reliability. From our initial discussions we understand the core issues to include:

Fragmented source of truth – Multiple systems (mentioned above) produce conflicting "headline" numbers for the same KPIs, with no single reconciled actuals dataset consumable by downstream reports or teams.

Manual, error-prone reconciliation processes – Org/account/segment mappings scattered across Excel files, plus manual CSV edits for eliminations and top-down adjustments, and inherited Power BI logic – all driving ~20-day CFO actuals close cycles and key-person dependency.

Mapping and ETL complexity – Incomplete mappings (especially business-group nuances), different transformation logic across pipelines, and legacy BPS constraints (quarterly inputs, 2-year horizon, aggregate org structure) prevent scalable, auditable group consolidation.

Limited scalability for future needs – Current Power BI reconciliation tool serves a small central team but will be difficult to evolve into the governed shared dataset business leaders are planning for, aligned to IBP changes, S/4HANA migration, and downstream planning/analytics use cases.

These challenges are particularly visible in the pipeline lifecycle, from opportunity creation to job roles, deal sheets, contracted backlog, and ultimately revenue recognition. While Salesforce captures significant operational detail, pipeline data is not integrated into core finance reporting and is not consistently trusted as a forward-looking revenue indicator. The absence of governance, stage definitions, reporting rules and a single source of truth for core commercial metrics makes the pipeline difficult to interpret and limits leadership’s ability to rely on it for forecasting and decision making.

Prescient has engaged JMAN to provide a proposal for an initial scope of work which seeks to establish a foundation for high-quality commercial and operational data to support business decision-making and prepare for an eventual transaction. This will focus on designing reporting solutions that provide clear visibility on growth drivers and value creation levers while addressing the data quality and reconciliation challenges that currently exist. There is particular interest in tracking sales and revenue across the molecule lifecycle with a forward-looking view on patent end dates, cross-selling and synergy benefits after acquisitions, and demonstrating the long-tenured, repeatable nature of client relationships. Whilst focusing on key growth drivers and transaction preparedness, the reporting solutions will ultimately deliver operational insights in the hands of the people who need data on a day-to-day basis.
